hook.line: The new waiter wants to know everything about Tomás, starting with coffee. Tomás loves it, but not after dark. Watch the little *el* appear in one half of his answer and vanish in the other.
hook.es: Me gusta el café, pero no tomo café por la noche.
hook.en: I like coffee, but I don't drink coffee at night.

examples.es: El trabajo es importante, pero la familia es más importante.
examples.en: Work is important, but family is more important.
Colombians drink a lot of black coffee.

examples.es: Los sábados trabajo en el café.
examples.en: On Saturdays I work in the café.

rule:
English and Spanish flip the switch the other way round.

For a thing in general, all coffee, work as such, Colombians as a whole, Spanish adds *el*, *la*, *los* or *las*, where English has nothing:
*Me gusta el café.* *El trabajo es importante.*

For some, an amount you don't count, Spanish has nothing, where English often says some or any:
*No tomo café por la noche.* *¿Hay pan?* *No tengo plata.*

So *compré pan* is I bought some bread, and *compré el pan* is I bought the bread, the one we both know about.

Three you've met already: jobs after *ser* go bare (*Soy ingeniero*), days take *el* or *los* (*los lunes*), hours take *la* or *las* (*Es la una*).

Quick test: if English could add in general, Spanish wants the article.
smallPrint: Teachers call the first one the generic use of the definite article, and a noun with no article at all a bare noun.

options: I drink the coffee every day.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *el café* or *café* and type the whole sentence: Me gusta ___.
yourTurn.why: Coffee in general takes *el* in Spanish.

yourTurn.prompt: Mariana's friend is an engineer. Choose *una ingeniera* or *ingeniera* and type the whole sentence: Es ___.
yourTurn.why: A job after *es* stands alone, with no *una*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I don't drink coffee at night.
yourTurn.answer: No tomo café por la noche.
accept: No tomo café en la noche.
yourTurn.why: Any coffee at all, an amount, so no article.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: On Saturdays I work in the café.
yourTurn.answer: Los sábados trabajo en el café.
accept: Trabajo en el café los sábados.
yourTurn.why: Every Saturday is *los sábados*, no word for on.

yourTurn.prompt: *Este tinto es fuerte* is about this cup. Make it about black coffee in general.
*Compré el pan* means the bread you'd talked about. Change it to just some bread.
yourTurn.why: Some bread, no particular loaf, so no article.

pitfalls.why: Almost. Coffee in general needs *el* in Spanish, even though English drops the.
After *soy*, the job stands alone, no *un*.
Dogs in general take *los* after *me gustan*.

pitfalls.wrong: Tomo el café todos los días.
pitfalls.why: With *el*, it's one particular coffee; for coffee as a habit, leave it out.

personal: Say something you like in general and something you never buy: *Me encanta el…*, *Nunca compro…*
